topics.label: Lecture framing and the cancer hallmarks framework
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the learning outcomes and the hallmarks framework that will organise the lecture.

topics.label: Mutational deregulation of growth and survival signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signalling pathways make cancer cells less dependent on normal growth controls.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in blood cancers and intestinal epithelium
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted differentiation sustains abnormal cell populations rather than normal tissue maturation.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how altered regulation of the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway allows cancer cells to avoid death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and replicative immortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the telomere-dependent limit on cell division and how cancer cells overcome it by reactivating telomerase.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the account of mutation-driven loss of growth control through an explanation of p53's protective responses and a recap of the hallmarks discussed.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and participates in a self-reinforcing relationship with genetic and epigenetic deregulation.

topics.label: Angiogenesis as a requirement for tumour growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the angiogenic switch supplies the perfusion needed for tumours to grow.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and successful secondary growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how cancer cells spread and what determines whether disseminated cells establish detectable tumours at secondary sites.

topics.label: Closing synthesis, further reading and questions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture's learning goals and shared cancer hallmarks before offering further reading and inviting questions.
